diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed every decisive fact (PF1–PF4) and cited all of them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed because of ENCODING MISMATCH on C2 and C4. C2 (linked to PF1, which requires naming the specific exposed data elements) failed in rollouts 1 and 3: the settlement decisions correctly set affected_record_count=2736, but the commitment detail text omitted the specific data-element combination ("names, email addresses, and unencrypted SSNs") that PF1's reveal contained, so the check found the settlement insufficient. C4 (linked to PF2, which requires the MA AG filing "no later than the same day as consumer notices") failed in rollout 1: the commitment used the shorthand "same-day filing requirement … alongside consumer notices" instead of the exact timing phrase the check expects. Rollout 0 and rollout 2 passed because their commitment details happened to include the full data-element list and the precise timing language.

C4.why: The ordinary draft does not require a Massachusetts Attorney General filing or specify its timing; PF2 changes the package to require that filing no later than the same day as consumer notices.

C2.why: The draft leaves the count undetermined and does not identify the exposed data elements; PF1 changes the filing to exactly 2,736 accounts and names the specific combination of exposed information.

For C2: either (a) add a dedicated decision field such as "exposed_data_elements" so the model must explicitly encode the data-element combination separately from the record count, ensuring C2 can match it regardless of commitment wording, or (b) relax C2 to accept any settlement whose justification_fact_ids include PF1 and whose affected_record_count equals 2736, without requiring the data elements to be restated in the commitment detail.
